_about: Gemma's lines for the recipe book (recipe-book-ux.md sections 7 and 8). Content editor owns the wording; docs/gemma-voice-guide.md applies. Where a value is a list, rotate without repeating in a visit. {placeholders} are filled by the page. Every line stays under 100 characters (the phone chat's Line size).

idea.first: I've had an idea for you. Tap it to have a look.
from_keep: That one gave me another idea.

keep._when: Speak on the 1st keep of the visit, the 3rd, then every 4th (7th, 11th...). Otherwise stay quiet: the animation and the live region are enough.
keep.first_ever: That's in your book now. It's up at the top, and it stays on this device.
first_this_visit: Kept. It's saved in your book.
third: Three in the book. I'm starting to see what you like.
Three kept. I'd say you're after {cluster_label}.

dismiss._when: Speak on the 1st dismiss of the visit only. After that, the undo line is enough.
dismiss.first: Fair enough. Fewer like that, then.

swipe_hint: Swipe right to keep one, or left if it's not for you.

book.full: Your book's full, so I've taken out the oldest one to make room.
book.no_storage: I can't keep a book on this device, so these are just for today.

theme._when: The book's This visit page, once something is kept this visit. Say `words` (if there are any) then one `kept_*` line. {words} = the theme words joined with `join`; {n} = the number kept, in words; {room} = the room's name as the dial shows it.
theme.words: This visit, by the look of it: {words}.
theme.kept_mixed: You've kept {n}, from around the Inn.

room_empty: That's everything I've got in here. Try next door.
diet_clash: I've taken the {title} away. It isn't {diet}.

write_out.remaining: Gemma writes it for you (3 a visit, {n} left).
write_out.remaining_one: Gemma writes it for you (3 a visit, one left).
write_out.at_cap: That's three recipes I've written this visit. The short version's above.
write_out.failed: My pen's run dry. The short version's above. Try again in a bit.

tell._about: Tell Gemma V1, keyed as tell.js and explore.html read them (tell-gemma/v1). {two} = the first two things, joined; {many} = 'A, b and a few more'; {c} = cuisines; {d} = diets; {p} = pantry words; {diet} and {room} as named. Every line stays under 100 characters.

pantry.title: What have you got to use?
pantry.privacy: Only used for Gemma's ideas and the recipes she writes for you.

dietary.title: Anything I should avoid?
dietary.otherNote: I'll pass that on when I write your recipe. I can't check my cards for it.
dietary.fodmapNote: I'll pass it on when I write your recipe. I only leave out cards I've checked.

ack.map: {c} it is. I'll lean that way.
ack.dietaryOther: Noted. I'll pass it on when I write your recipe.

entry.dietary: I'll keep to {d} in here too.
entry.pantry: I'll look for things that use your {p}.

tell.offer: Want to tell me what's in your cupboard, or anything to avoid?
tell.nothingAnywhere: I can't find anything on my shelves that fits all of that.
tell.roomNone: Nothing in here fits {diet}, I'm afraid. {room} has a few.
tell._countries: The Map's select, with a one-line example of the shopping words under it (tell-gemma-ux.md §3).
tell._synonyms: word → words that mean the same; a pantry word matches an atom when it or one of these is in its key_ingredients (after singularising).
tell._why: Reasons for the navigator's 'Because you …' line, when a pantry or cuisine match is the strongest reason.

objects.pantry-cabinet: Tell me what's in the cupboard, and I'll cook around it.
objects.locale-map: Pick a few places to cook from, and where you do your shopping.
objects.dietary-shelf: Tell me what to steer clear of, and I'll keep to it.

tell._objects: Gemma's line when the visitor touches the object, as its sheet opens (optional).

checkin._about: The check-in sheet (Ideas build, checkin-build). One wording set per answer for every door. {t} {n} {c} are filled from the option labels below, lower-cased mid-sentence. Every line under 100 characters.
checkin.title: Check in
checkin.helper: All optional. Skip anything you like.

rows.servings: How many are you cooking for?
rows.confidence: How do you feel in the kitchen?

checkin.confidenceHelper: This is about skill. Your candle is about today.

ack._when: One line on Done, only if something changed. Energy uses the candle's own moment.
ack.checkin: Thanks. I'll keep all that in mind.
ack.servings: Cooking for {n}. I'll do the maths.
ack.servingsOne: Just you. I'll keep it small.
ack.confidence: {c}. I'll pitch the recipes to suit.
ack.checkinTwo: {a}, and {b}. I'll keep all that in mind.

ask._when: Gemma's one gentle ask per visit, for one missing answer, only when it would change her picks.
ask.time: How long have you got? It changes what I'd pick.
ask.servings: How many are you cooking for? I'll scale the recipe.
ask.confidence: How do you feel in the kitchen? I'll pitch the recipe to suit.

checkin._about: The foyer check-in pieces outside the sheet (checkin-views.md): the opener (front door) and the desk and groceries hotspots. The sheet copy is tell.checkin.

opener.welcome: Have a wander. Start at the desk if you like.
opener.line: Hello, love. Want to check in? It helps me pick for you.

desk.label: The front desk
desk.moment: Sign in if you like. It helps me pick, and none of it is kept.

groceries.label: The groceries
groceries.moment: What did you bring in? Tell me and I'll cook around it.

chia._about: The Chiapothecary's moods and Mix an experiment (rooms-views.md, stage A), keyed as the Ideas build reads them (rooms-chia). Moods, not medicine: each says what's in it, never what it does. Swap lines are food facts only; first match wins, one at a time, never blocking. Every line under 100 characters ({x} {m} {n} filled by the page).

morning-spark.label: Morning spark
morning-spark.inIt: Matcha, citrus and a spoon of peanut butter.

deep-focus.label: Deep focus
deep-focus.inIt: Walnuts, blueberries and a little cacao.

cultured.label: Cultured
cultured.inIt: Kefir or yoghurt, with kiwifruit and oats.

by-flavour.label: By flavour
by-flavour.inIt: Just whatever tastes good to you.

swaps.line: Kefir is what makes it cultured. Would you try kefir instead?
Kefir is what makes it cultured. Would you try kefir instead?
Lemon can split milk overnight. Coconut milk stays smooth. Would you try coconut milk instead?
Lemon can curdle soy milk overnight. Oat milk stays smooth. Would you try oat milk instead?
Kefir is already tangy, and matcha adds bitterness. Would you try vanilla instead?
Matcha has caffeine. Chamomile is part of what Calm is made of. Would you try chamomile instead?
Cacao nibs have a little caffeine. Would you try toasted coconut instead?
Matcha is the one with caffeine, and Morning spark is built around it. Would you try matcha instead?
Walnuts are part of what Deep focus is made of. Would you try walnuts instead?
Kiwifruit is part of what Bright is made of. Would you try kiwifruit instead?
Granola goes soft overnight, so add it just before you eat.

lines.moodHelper: Each one is a set of ingredients. What it does for you is your call.
lines.mixIntro: Four choices, then I'll write up the recipe.
lines.prefill: I've started with what you picked from the drawers and the fridge.

steps.base: What shall we set it in?

lines.swapped: Swapped. I think you'll like it.
lines.cap: Gemma writes it for you (3 a visit, {n} left).
lines.capNone: That's three recipes written this visit. The jar's short version is still yours.
lines.breakfastLine: Set it tonight and it's ready by morning.
lines.breakfastLineDay: Set it now and it'll be ready by 7 tomorrow morning.
lines.jarsLine: Four jars, one batch. That's most of the week sorted.
lines.jarsChanged: Four jars, so I've made it four, not {n}. I've scaled your list.

sweet._about: Sweet Spells (rooms-views.md, stage B). How sweet and sweeteners are Inn-wide answers (the Chiapothecary uses them too). Atoms carry `sweetener` (sugar, honey, maple, agave, dates, fruit) and `added_sugar` (true for honey, maple, sugar, agave, chocolate or granola; false for fruit and dates, assuming plain peanut butter and unsweetened milks). Every line under 100 characters.

sweetenWith.title: Sweeten with…
sweetenWith.helper: Only if you'd like less sugar. Pick any.

occasions.title: What's it for?
occasions.helper: I'll suggest how many and how long, unless you've already told me.

tea.label: Afternoon tea
tea.line: Afternoon tea. Something to share with a cuppa.

dinner.label: A dinner party
dinner.line: A dinner party. A pudding for six, I'd say.

celebration.label: A celebration
celebration.line: A celebration. Let's make it look the part.

howSweet.less: A bit less sugar. I'll go gently.
howSweet.none: No added sugar. Fruit can do the work.

swap._when: On Sweet Spells recipe pages, when the visitor's sweetener differs from the recipe's. Checked kitchen guidance, not invented ratios.
swap.title: Swap the sugar

rules.line: Use about ¾ as much maple syrup, and a little less of any other liquid.
Use about ¾ as much honey and a little less liquid. It browns faster, so bake a bit cooler.
rules.noBake: Use about ¾ as much honey and a little less liquid.

rules.line: Use about ⅔ as much agave, and a little less of any other liquid.
Blend soft dates to a paste, about the same amount as the sugar. Best in puddings, not crisp bakes.
Swap one for one. Maple is a little thinner and not quite as sweet.
Swap one for one. Honey is a little sweeter, so a touch less is fine.
Swap one for one. Agave is runnier, so drizzle it rather than spoon it.
Swap one for one. Agave is a little sweeter.
Swap one for one. Maple is a little thicker and not quite as sweet.
Follow the packet. Sweeteners vary a lot in strength, and some don't brown or bake like sugar.
Leave it out and let ripe fruit do the work. It will be less sweet.
